requests.get is ALWAYS sending content length
Hi,

It seems like that request.get always adds 'content-length' header to the request.
I think that the right behavior is not to add this header automatically in GET requests or add the possibility to not send it.

For example http://amazon.com returns 503 for every get request that contains 'content-length' header.

Thanks,

Oren

The issue is in the `prepare_content_length` method at line 388-395. It always sets `Content-Length` to `'0'` even when the body is `None`. For GET requests (and other methods that typically don't have a body), the body is `None`, but `Content-Length: 0` is still being set.

The fix should be: if body is `None`, don't set `Content-Length` at all.

Now I can see the issue. In `prepare_content_length`, the first line unconditionally sets `Content-Length` to `'0'`, even when the body is `None`. For GET requests without a body, this means a `Content-Length: 0` header is always sent.
The fix: only set `Content-Length` when there's actually a body. If body is `None`, don't set `Content-Length` at all.
